title: GOODMORNING JESUS
text: Hallelujah. Come on, lift your voice and give him praise right now. Come on, worship him. Worship him from that place in your spirit where words almost fail you. Worship him because he's worthy. Not because of what he has done alone, but because of who he is. Hallelujah. Glory to God. Be seated in his presence. Father, we say good morning to you. We open our eyes and the first thing we want to see is your face. The first voice we want to hear [music] is yours. The first presence we want to feel is the warmth of your spirit wrapping around us like a garment. Jesus. Good morning, Lord. We are here. We are present. We are [music] awake and we are yours. Have your way in this place. Amen. I want to begin this morning by asking you a question and I want you to really think about it. I do not want you to give me a religious answer. I want a real answer from the depths of your heart. What is the first thing you do when you wake up in the morning? What is the very first thought that occupies your mind when consciousness returns to you and you realize that God has [music] granted you another day? Because that first moment, that first breath of a new day, that transition from sleep to waking, it is one of the most spiritually significant moments of your entire day and most believers are wasting it. Most people wake up and the first thing they reach for is a phone. They scroll through notifications. They check messages. They look at what happened in the world while they were sleeping. They fill their minds with information, with noise, with the concerns of the day before they have even given Jesus a single moment of their morning. And I want to tell you today that this is one of the greatest strategies of the enemy against the modern believer. He does not need to come at you with some dramatic demonic attack [music] in the morning. All he needs to do is keep your attention on anything other than Jesus in that first sacred window of the day and he has already won a significant battle over the atmosphere of your entire day. Turn with me to the book of Psalms. Psalm 5 and verse 3. David says, "My voice you shall hear in the morning, oh Lord. In the morning I will direct it to you and I will look up." My voice you shall hear in the morning. David made a decision. This was not an accident. This was not something that happened when circumstances aligned. This was a deliberate, intentional, covenantal decision that David made about the posture of his mornings. He said, "In the morning, not in the afternoon, not when I feel like it, not after I have handled my business, not after I have checked my status among the people. In the morning, first before anything else, before any other voice gets my ear, you, Lord, shall have my voice." And then notice what he says, "I will direct it to you." The word direct in the Hebrew is arak and it means to set in order, to arrange, to marshal, like a military commander marshaling his forces. David is saying, "I will marshal my prayer toward you in the morning. I will arrange my heart. I will set my spirit in order and aim everything at you before the day has a chance to pull me in a hundred different directions." And then [music] he says, "I will look up." After I have directed my prayer toward you, I will [music] look up in anticipation. I will wait in expectation because I know that the God who hears [music] prayer is faithful to answer. This is the lifestyle of a person who walks in consistent victory. This is the rhythm of a life that is hidden in Christ. Morning by morning, first thing, Jesus gets the firstfruits of your [music] consciousness, of your attention, of your affection, of your worship. And when Jesus [music] gets the first of your day, he sanctifies the rest of it. When you consecrate your morning to him, he covers the afternoon. When you give him the first hour, he orders the remaining hours. This is not a formula. This is a spiritual principle rooted in the nature of God and the way covenant works. Let me take you to another scripture. Mark chapter 1 and verse 35. This is one of the most powerful verses in the New Testament and [music] most people read it too quickly. The Bible says, "Now in the morning, having risen a long while before daylight, he went out and departed to a solitary place and there he prayed." Who is the he? Jesus, the son of God, the word made flesh. The one through whom all things were created, the one in whom all the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily. [music] This Jesus woke up a long while before daylight and went to a solitary [music] place to pray. I need you to sit with that for a moment. Why would Jesus need to pray? Why would the son of God, who had authority over demons, who raised the dead, who stilled storms with his voice, why would he need to rise before dawn and go into a solitary place to commune with the Father? Because prayer was not just about asking for things. Prayer was the lifeline of connection between the son and the Father. Prayer was the place where Jesus received his assignment for the day. Prayer was where he downloaded heaven's agenda. Prayer was where he drew from the infinite resources of divinity to fuel his humanity. And if the son of God, the most anointed human being who ever walked the face of this earth, prioritized morning communion with the Father, what does that say about your need and my need to do the same? You cannot afford to start your day without Jesus. You literally cannot afford it. The cost of [music] a prayerless morning is too high. Because when you step out into the day without first connecting with heaven, you step out uncovered, you step out unequipped. You step out with your own wisdom, your own strength, your own understanding, and the The says in Proverbs 3 and verse 5, "Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding." A morning without prayer is a morning where you have decided, consciously or unconsciously, to lean on your own understanding. And your own understanding is not enough for what this day holds. Let me show you something in Isaiah. Isaiah 50 and verse 4. The Lord G O D has given me the tongue of the learned that I should know how to speak a word in season to him who is weary. He awakens me morning by morning. >> [music] >> He awakens my ear to hear as the learned. This is a prophetic utterance pointing to the Messiah, but there is a principle here that belongs to every child [music] of God. He awakens me morning by morning to hear. To hear what? To hear the voice of God, to receive instruction, to get direction, to be aligned with the divine agenda for that specific day. God wants to awaken your ear every morning. He wants to speak to you before the world speaks to you. He wants to give you your assignment before your inbox gives you someone else's agenda. He wants to fill you with his word before the news fills you with fear. Morning by morning, this is not a special privilege for prophets and apostles. This is the inheritance of every son and daughter of God. Now, I want to talk to you about what the morning actually represents spiritually. The morning is not just a time of day. In scripture, morning carries a specific theological weight. Psalm 30 and verse 5 says, "Weeping may endure for a night, but joy comes in the morning." Morning is the symbol of divine intervention after a season of darkness. [music] Morning represents the faithfulness of God. Lamentations 3 and verses 22 and 23 says, "The steadfast love of the Lord never ceases. His mercies never come to an end. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness." New every morning. Think about that. [music] Every time the sun rises, God is releasing fresh mercy over your life. Every morning that you wake up, there is a new consignment of divine grace available to you. Mercy that was not available yesterday. Grace that is specifically calibrated for today. Strength that has been freshly issued from the throne room of heaven for the challenges and the opportunities and the assignments of this specific day. And the question is, are you accessing it? Are you showing up in the morning to receive what God [music] has already prepared for you? The enemy works hardest at night. The Bible says in Matthew 13 and verse [music] 25 that while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat. While men slept, the enemy uses the night season. He plants seeds of fear, seeds of anxiety, seeds of confusion, seeds of discouragement while you are in rest. And that is why it is so critical that when you wake up, the first thing you do is run into the presence of God. Because the morning is where God reverses [music] what the enemy did in the night. The morning is where confusion is replaced by clarity, where anxiety is replaced by peace, where fear is replaced by faith, where heaviness is replaced by joy. The morning encounter with Jesus is the antidote to everything the enemy planted while you were sleeping. I want to tell you about the mercy seat. The tabernacle of Moses, and this is deeply significant, was oriented toward the east. The entrance faced east, toward the morning sun. Toward the place where light first [music] breaks through darkness. This was not architectural coincidence. This was a prophetic statement. God was saying the way you enter my presence is from the direction of the morning. From the direction of new beginnings, from the direction of fresh light. Every morning is an invitation to enter the presence of God as if it were the first time, with fresh wonder, with fresh hunger, with fresh expectancy. Somebody is here today and your mornings have become mechanical. You have a routine. You might even have a devotional. You read a scripture, you say a quick prayer, you go about your day, but there is no fire. There is no encounter. There is no sense of the weight of glory. Your morning time with God has become a religious ritual rather than a relational encounter. And today God is calling you back. He's calling you back to that place of genuine communion. To that place where you wake up and you literally talk to him, not recite things at him, not perform spiritual activities in his general direction, but talk to him like a friend, [music] like a father, like a savior, like a king. Good morning, Jesus. I am here. What do you want to say to me today? What do you want to do in me today? What do you need me to know before this day begins? Let me take you to Song of Solomon chapter 3 and verse 1. The Shulamite says, "By night on my bed I sought the one I love. I sought him, but I did not find him. I will rise now, I said, and go about the city in the streets and in the squares I will seek the one I love." This is a picture of a soul that is desperate [music] for communion with Christ. A soul that cannot be satisfied with second-hand experiences. A soul that refuses to be content with anything less than the presence of the beloved. And notice [music] she says, "I will rise now." There is a rising that is connected to seeking. There is a getting up that is motivated by love, not by obligation, not by religious duty, but by the [music] desperate burning, consuming desire to be in the presence [music] of the one has so loves. That is what morning prayer was designed to be. Not a duty you perform before you can legitimately go about your day. Not a spiritual tax you pay to God so that you will bless what you are about to do. Morning prayer is a love encounter. [music] It is the meeting of a longing soul with a waiting God. God waits for you every morning. Before you open your eyes, he's already there. Before you form the first thought, his presence is already filling the room. He does not need to be summoned. He does not need to be convinced to show up. He's already there. The question is whether you will turn toward him or turn away. Revelation 3 and verse 20, Jesus says, "Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come into him and dine with him and he with me." He is standing at the door. Right now, this morning, he's not far away. He's not occupied with more important things. He's not distracted by the affairs of running the universe. He's standing [music] at the door of your morning. He is knocking. He's saying, "Let me in. Give me this moment. Give me this first breath. Give me this first hour." And if you open the door, he will come in. And the word dine in that verse is not casual eating. It is the Greek word deipnon, which refers [music] to the main meal of the day. The most substantial, most intimate, most meaningful meal. God is saying, "If you open the door in the morning, I will not give you a snack. I will not give you a quick bite. I will come in and I will give you a feast. I will nourish your spirit. I will feed [music] your soul. I will sustain you with the bread of heaven that the world cannot give and the world cannot take away." I need to talk to you about what happens spiritually when you begin [music] your day with Jesus because it is not just about your personal spiritual health, though that matters enormously. When you begin your day in his presence, there is a covering that comes upon your life that cannot be explained in natural terms. Psalm 91 and verse 1 says, "He who dwells in the secret place of the most high shall abide under the shadow of the almighty." The secret place is a morning encounter. It is a daily to the presence. And the promise attached to that consistent dwelling in His presence is abiding, remaining, staying under the shadow of the Almighty. What is the shadow of the Almighty? It is divine protection. It is supernatural covering. It is the canopy of heaven stretched over your life as you walk through a world that is full of danger, full of uncertainty, [music] full of darkness. You want to know why some believers seem to walk in a different [music] kind of protection. You want to know why trouble seems to pass over certain people. You want to know why some people go through impossible situations and come out untouched. It is not luck. It is not mere chance. It is the [music] shadow of the Almighty. And that shadow is accessed through the secret place, through the morning encounter, through the daily, deliberate, passionate return to His presence. When the enemy looks at a person who has been in the secret place that morning, he sees a covering over them that makes him back away. He sees the fingerprints of God on their life. He sees the fire of the Holy Spirit surrounding them like a wall, and he has to go look for someone who woke up and skipped their morning. I want to share something with you now that I believe is going to bring liberation to many people here. There is a lie that many believers have accepted about their morning time with God. The lie says that the quality of your morning devotion is measured by the length of time you spend or by the spiritual intensity of the experience you have. So, if you spend 45 minutes but did not cry, if you spent an hour but did not feel goosebumps, if you prayed but the heavens felt like brass, [music] you conclude that your morning was a failure. That you did not really connect, that God was not pleased, and then guilt sets in. And guilt about yesterday's morning makes you approach today's morning with a spirit of condemnation rather than a spirit of faith. And condemnation never produces intimacy. Condemnation drives you away from the presence rather than drawing you into it. The truth is this. Your morning encounter with God is not measured by feelings. It is measured by faith. Hebrews 11 and verse 6 says without faith it is impossible to please God. For he who comes to God must believe that he is and that he is a rewarder of those who diligently seek him. The key is not the emotional temperature of the encounter. The key is the faith of the one who comes. Did you come believing he is there? Did you come expecting him to answer? Did you open your mouth and speak to him as a real person and not as an abstract theological concept? Did you open the word and receive it as his actual voice speaking directly to you in this moment? If you came with faith, if you came with expectancy, [music] if you came with a genuine desire to know him and not just to complete a spiritual exercise, that morning was received by heaven. That morning was honored by the one who sees in secret and rewards [music] openly. Let me tell you about the manna. Exodus 16. When Israel was in the wilderness, God provided manna every morning. Every single morning, fresh bread from heaven fell on the ground around the camp of Israel. >> [music] >> And the instructions were specific. You had to go out and gather it in the morning because by the time the sun grew hot it was gone. You could not collect tomorrow's manna today. You could not store up last week's supply and live on it this week. Every morning was a fresh requirement for a fresh gathering. And what was not gathered in the morning was not available later. I want to suggest to you that spiritual manna works the same way. The fresh bread of heaven, the fresh word, the fresh instruction, the fresh anointing, the fresh grace that God wants to release into your life is available in the morning. Every morning there is a fresh consignment of grace from heaven specifically designed for that day. And if you do not gather it in your morning encounter, you'll go into the day without the provision that was prepared for you. You go without the instruction you needed. You make decisions without the wisdom that was available. You face battles without the strength that was already issued to you. Not because God withheld it, but because you did not go out and gather in the morning. Proverbs 8 and verse 17 says, "I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently will find me." Diligently. The word diligently in the Hebrew is shakar, and it literally means to seek early in the morning. It means to be up at dawn looking. It means to make the morning the time of your most earnest, [music] most focused, most determined seeking. And the promise attached to this early seeking, this morning diligence, is I will be [music] found. God says if you seek me this way, in this posture, with this kind of dedication and intentionality, you will find me. Not maybe, >> [music] >> not sometimes, you will find me. It is a divine guarantee attached to a morning discipline. There is somebody listening to this right now, and God has been trying to get your attention in the morning for weeks. He has been waking you up early. >> [music] >> You have been waking up at 3:00, 4:00, 5:00 in the morning, and you have been turning over and going back to sleep, [music] and you have been attributing it to stress, or insomnia, or the neighbor's noise. But I want to tell you today that the Holy Spirit has been nudging you. He has been interrupting your sleep because he has something to say to you, [music] and the only time he can get you without distraction is in the early hours before the world wakes up. And he's saying to you right now, "Do not go back to sleep. Come. Come and meet with me. Come and receive what I've been trying to give you. Come into the secret place and let me show you what I see. Let me tell you what I know. Let me speak over your life and your situation from the perspective of eternity. I want to talk briefly about the power of morning declarations. Job 22 and verse 28 says, "You will also declare a thing and it will be established for you." The morning is the time for declarations. Before the enemy has a chance to set the agenda, before fear has a chance to plant its seed, you open your mouth and you declare what the word of God says about your day. You declare the promises. You declare the character of God. You call the day into alignment with divine purpose. You speak to your body. You speak to your mind. You speak to your relationships. You speak to your finances. You speak to everything that is under your jurisdiction as a child of God and you say, "This day belongs to God. This day is ordered by the Lord. I am covered by the blood of Jesus. I am filled with the spirit of God. I am guided by the wisdom of heaven. No weapon formed against me today shall prosper. Every tongue that rises against me today shall be condemned. The plans of God for my life are good plans. Plans for peace and not for evil. Plans for a future and a hope. I receive them in Jesus' name." When you begin your day with declarations like this, you are not just speaking positive affirmations. You are not doing spiritual psychology. You are releasing something into the spiritual atmosphere that goes ahead of you and begins to arrange the day according to what you have declared. Angels hearken to the voice of his word. Psalm 103 and verse 20. When you speak the word, [music] when you make morning declarations rooted in scripture, angels are activated. They go ahead of you. They begin to to the way. They begin to enforce the word you have declared. And by the time you step out of your house, your way has already been prepared by unseen hands responding to your morning declarations. I want to pray with you now, but before I do, I want you to do something. Take a moment and make this decision. Not just for today, not for this week, make a covenant with yourself and with God that from this day forward, the first voice that gets your attention in the morning will be his. Before you pick up a phone, before you turn on a television, before you scroll or read or check anything, you will say good morning, Jesus. You will open your heart. You will give him the first moments and watch how your days begin to change. Watch how the atmosphere of your life shifts. Watch how clarity comes where there was confusion. Watch how peace replaces anxiety. Watch how provision shows up in unexpected places. Watch how divine connections walk into your life out of nowhere. Not because you became more talented or more strategic or more fortunate, but because you gave God the morning and the morning gave him legal access to the rest of your day. Share this with someone today. Somebody in your life needs to hear this. Somebody you know has been struggling with their morning. Somebody you know has been waking up already overwhelmed, already defeated, already behind before the day begins. Share this with them. The word of God is a seed and every seed carries life and every life carries the potential for transformation. Share it before we go into prayer. Let the word go forth. Now, lift your hands wherever you are. Every hand lifted, every heart [music] open. Whether you are in this building or you are watching from somewhere in the world, whether it is morning where you are or evening or the middle of the night, God is not bound by time zones. His presence is available right now. Lift your hands and let us enter into his presence together. Father, we say good morning. Good morning to the King of kings. Good morning to the Lord of lords. Good morning to the lamb that was slain and lives forevermore. [music] Good morning to the ancient of days. Good morning to the lily of the valley, the bright and morning star, the son of righteousness who rises with healing in his wings. We greet you this morning, Lord. We acknowledge you. We recognize your presence. [music] We say thank you for another day. Thank you for another breath. Thank you for the mercy that brought us through the night and the grace that meets us in this morning. Holy Spirit, we welcome you afresh. Come and move in this atmosphere right now. Come and minister to every dry and thirsty soul. Come and feed every person who came hungry. Come and strengthen every person who came [music] weary. Come and speak to every person who came confused and uncertain and needing a word from heaven. Come, Holy Spirit. We need you. We are nothing without you. We can do nothing without you, but with you all things are possible and every promise is yes and amen. Come, Lord. Now I pray for everyone in this place and everyone connected right now. I break [music] the power of morning heaviness in the name of Jesus. That spirit that makes people wake up already burdened, already pressed, [music] already feeling the weight of everything that is unresolved and everything [music] that is uncertain. I come against that spirit right now with the authority of the name that is above every name, the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. Be broken, be lifted, be dissolved in the presence of the living God. I release the spirit of joy. I release the spirit of praise. I release a fresh visitation of the Holy Spirit over every morning from this day forward. Father, I pray that you would give every believer a fresh hunger for the morning. Awaken in them a longing for your presence that is stronger than their longing for sleep. Awaken in them an appetite for your word that is more urgent than their appetite [music] for food. Create in every person connected right now a holy restlessness that will not let them be satisfied with anything less than a genuine encounter with you in the morning hours. Give them the discipline, Lord. Give them the desire. Give them the fire. Let the Holy Spirit be the alarm clock that wakes them into your presence. I speak to every dry season right now. Every person whose prayer life has become routine, whose morning devotion has become mechanical, whose passion for the presence has grown cold through the business of life and the pleasures of the season. I declare reversal right now. I declare rekindling right now. Like the fire on the altar that was never allowed to go out, I declare that the fire of God is being reignited in every heart. The embers that the enemy tried to extinguish are being fanned into flame right now by the breath of the Holy Spirit. For every person who has been waking up afraid, who opens their eyes and the first thing that hits them [music] is anxiety about the future, anxiety about provision, anxiety about health, anxiety about relationships. I rebuke that spirit of fear right now. 2 Timothy 1 and verse 7 says God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind. I decree that power over every fearful [music] morning. I decree love over every anxious morning. I decree a sound mind over every morning that has been hijacked by worry and dread. You will wake up with peace. You will wake up with clarity. You will wake up with the assurance that the God who held you through the night [music] is more than capable of carrying you through the day. Receive that in Jesus' name. I speak to every promise [music] that was given in a morning encounter with God and has not yet manifested. Every word that was received in the secret place, every dream that came in the night season carrying a divine message, every vision that broke in on the early hours of morning, I declare those promises are still alive. They have not expired. God has not forgotten them. They are preserved in heaven. They are held in the hands of the almighty. And in the fullness of time, at the appointed season, [music] they will burst forth into manifestation with a glory that will cause you to stand in awe. For the sick, I release healing right now. The sun of righteousness rises with healing in his wings. This is a morning scripture, Malachi 4 and verse 2. Every morning that you rise and say good morning, Jesus, you are welcoming the sun of righteousness whose wings carry healing. So, I declare healing in your body right now. I declare healing in your mind right now. Whatever disease has been lodged in your body, whatever infirmity has been resisting the word of God, I come against it right now with the authority of heaven, and I declare its eviction. It has no legal right to remain in the temple of the Holy Spirit. Leave now in the name of Jesus. The body belongs [music] to God. The body is the temple of the Holy Spirit, and no infirmity has squatting rights in the temple of God. Be healed. Be whole. Be restored. From the crown of your head to the soles of your feet, I declare divine health in Jesus' name. For every person who has been praying about a door that will not open, a door of opportunity, a door of advancement, a door of divine connection, I speak to that door right now. Revelation 3 and verse 8 says, "I have set before you an open door, and no one can shut it." That door is open. It has been opened by the one who holds the keys of David. What he opens, no man shuts. What he shuts, no man opens. And the doors that God has ordained for your life are standing open right now, waiting for you to walk through them in faith. Step through in Jesus name. Walk into what God has prepared. Walk into the next level. Walk into the season of fulfillment. Walk into everything that has been reserved for you since before the foundation of the world. Now Father, we declare over this day. We declare it is a good day. It is a day that the Lord has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it. We declare that your hand goes before us. >> [music] >> Your angels encamp around us. Your favor surrounds us like a shield. Your wisdom guides our steps. Your word lights our path. We will not stumble. We will not fall. We will not be overtaken by the enemy. We will not be overwhelmed by the pressure of this world. Because you are with us. Emmanuel God with us. The same God who walked with Adam in the garden. The same God who was with Joseph in the pit and in the prison and in the palace. The same God who walked with the three Hebrew boys in the fire. That God is with us right now. In this morning, in this day, in this season. And his presence makes all the difference. Good morning, Jesus. We love you. We worship you. We give you this day. All of it. Every hour, every moment, every opportunity, every challenge, every conversation, every decision. We surrender it all to you. Order our steps. Align our path. Let your will be done in our lives on earth as it is in heaven. And at the end of this day when we lay our heads down to rest, let us be able to look back and see the fingerprints of God all over everything that happened. In Jesus mighty name.
